title: In-between Transatlantic (Monetary) Disturbances
hypothesis: ECB contractionary monetary policy shocks spill over to Canada via trade/commodity (oil) channels with limited financial spillovers; Fed shocks tighten Canadian financial conditions with broader slower real effects; magnitudes comparable and distinct transmission mechanisms
data_sources: Large Canadian Database for Macroeconomic Analysis Fortin et al. 2022
IMF-IFS database for CAD/EUR exchange rate
Federal Reserve Excess Bond Premium Gilchrist and Zakrajsek 2012
Eurostat sts_inpr_m production in industry Short-term business statistics
ICE BofA Euro High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread BAMLHE00EHYIOAS
sample: Canadian small open economy. Canadian variables from Large Canadian Database for Macroeconomic Analysis of Fortin et al. 2022 (CAD/EUR from IMF-IFS): nominal exchange rate (against USD for Fed, against EUR for ECB), Bank of Canada policy rate, CPI, equity price index, monthly GDP index . US variables from St. Louis FRED and Federal Reserve: federal funds rate, industrial production index, PCE price index, Excess Bond Premium of Gilchrist and Zakrajsek 2012 . Euro Area variables from FRED and Eurostat sts_inpr_m: ECB main refinancing rate, industrial production index, HICP, ICE BofA Euro High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread BAMLHE00EHYIOAS . Augmented variables: oil GDP value added, oil production cubic meters, non-oil GDP, oil exports, non-oil exports, WTI oil price; seven export categories; five GDP components; US spillover variables; financial-price variables; all added one at a time. Identification events: ECB (blue) and Fed (red) monetary policy announcements. Sample sizes N observations / N shocks: not stated - the paper does not print number of months, observations or announcement counts.
period_end: not stated - full sample end date not printed; COVID dummy covers March 2020–June 2021; robustness truncated sample ends February 2020
method: 1. Collect Canadian, US and Euro Area variables as above with sources Fortin et al. 2022, IMF-IFS, FRED, Federal Reserve EBP, Eurostat.
2. Measure high-frequency surprises in interest rates and equity prices around ECB and Fed policy announcement windows (window length not stated).

3. Separate pure monetary policy shock from central bank information disclosure shock via Jarocinski 2022 rotational-angle decomposition searching over rotations consistent with sign restrictions (contractionary MP shock: rates up, equities down). Benchmark uses median rotation among admissible rotations; display shock series in Fig3 and Fig4.

4. Bayesian VAR: endogenous variables with 3 lags (footnote compromise between AIC 4 lags and BIC 2 lags), exogenous identified ECB and Fed MP shocks, linear time trend, COVID dummy March 2020–June 2021. Normal-Wishart prior per Dieppe et al. 2016 BEAR: prior mean for first own lag 0.8, overall tightness lambda1 0.1, lag decay lambda3 1. Diffuse priors for exogenous shocks. Compute median IRF and 90% posterior credible intervals per horizon h.

5. Local projections per Equation eq:LP_Benchmark: y_t+h = beta_Shock_h i_t^Shock + sum j=1..J_i phi i_t-j + sum delta y_t-j + sum alpha x_t-j + sum alpha* x*_t-j + gamma1 Trend + gamma2 CovidDummy + epsilon, with 3 lags of y, x, x*, and shocks (AIC-selected), Trend and CovidDummy. Standard errors clustered at time level, 90% confidence intervals. Under standard assumptions VAR and LP identify same population response.

6. Transmission channels: re-estimate benchmark VAR augmented with oil/trade variables (oil GDP value added, oil production cubic meters, non-oil GDP, oil exports, non-oil exports, WTI oil price), with seven export categories one at a time, with GDP components, and with financial-price variables (government bond yields 1-3yr, 3-5yr, 10+yr, 1-year mortgage rate, New Housing Price Index). Also estimate responses of US economy (industrial production, PCE price index, excess bond premium, federal funds rate) to ECB shock and Canadian bilateral trade flows with US and EU. Shock normalization for US figures: one-standard-deviation ECB pure monetary policy shock.

7. Robustness: Poor Man's Sign Restriction (Jarocinski 2020 central) classifying negative rate-equity co-movement as MP shock and positive as information shock; local projection median rotation; sample excluding COVID ending February 2020; integrating over identification uncertainty by normalizing admissible rotations to 999 angles and taking repeated random uniform draws, constructing pointwise 90% credible bands combining posterior and identification uncertainty.
